proposals.before: Early in the Wude era he sent envoys to submit to the court and was appointed Qaghan Tuwuoguo Ba, receiving generous reassurance.
proposals.after: Early in the Wude era he sent envoys to submit to the court and was appointed Qaghan Tuwuoguo Baque, receiving generous reassurance.
proposals.reason: The Chinese title is 吐烏過拔闕可汗; the rendering 'Tuwuoguo Ba' omits the final element 闕 (que), so the qaghan title is truncated.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Wude he sent envoys to submit inwardly and was appointed Qaghan Tuwuoguo Ba; he was treated with generous reassurance.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Wude he sent envoys to submit inwardly and was appointed Qaghan Tuwuoguo Baque; he was treated with generous reassurance.
proposals.reason: The Chinese title is 吐烏過拔闕可汗; the rendering 'Tuwuoguo Ba' omits the final element 闕 (que), so the qaghan title is truncated.

proposals.before: Qaghan Jieli resented China's marriage alliance with him and repeatedly sent troops to raid; he also sent word to Tongyehu, saying, "If you welcome a Tang princess, you must pass through my territory."
proposals.after: Qaghan Jieli resented China's marriage alliance with Tongyehu and repeatedly sent troops to raid; he also sent word to Tongyehu, saying, "If you welcome a Tang princess, you must pass through my territory."
proposals.reason: In 與之和親 the pronoun 之 refers to Tongyehu (the marriage partner discussed in s0058-s0063); 'with him' after the subject Jieli wrongly reads as Jieli himself.

proposals.before: Eastward the Ili River was the boundary; from Kucha, Shanshan, Qiemo, Tokhara, Yanqi, Shiguo, Shiguo of the Shi, Heguo, Muguo, and Kangguo, all were under his command.
proposals.after: Eastward the Ili River was the boundary; from Kucha, Shanshan, Qiemo, Tokhara, Yanqi, Shiguo, the Shi state, Heguo, Muguo, and Kangguo, all were under his command.
proposals.reason: The list reads 石國、史國; 'Shiguo of the Shi' garbles 史國 (the Shi state), a distinct state from 石國 Shiguo.

proposals.before: Shidianmi had followed the chanyu in commanding the ten great chieftains; with an army of one hundred thousand he pacified the Hu states of the Western Regions, set himself up as qaghan, and was called the Ten Surname Tribes, ruling their people for generations.
proposals.after: Shidianmi had followed the chanyu in commanding the ten great chieftains; with an army of one hundred thousand he pacified the Hu states of the Western Regions and set himself up as qaghan; his people were called the Ten Surname Tribes, and his line ruled them for generations.
proposals.reason: 號十姓部落，世統其眾 names the people as the Ten Surname Tribes and says his line ruled them for generations; the English wrongly makes Shidianmi himself 'called the Ten Surname Tribes'.

proposals.before: At first Shidianmi followed the chanyu in commanding the ten great chieftains; he had an army of one hundred thousand men, went to pacify the various Hu states of the Western Regions, set himself up as qaghan, and was called the Ten Surname Tribes, ruling their masses for generations.
proposals.after: At first Shidianmi followed the chanyu in commanding the ten great chieftains; he had an army of one hundred thousand men, went to pacify the various Hu states of the Western Regions, set himself up as qaghan, and [his people] were called the Ten Surname Tribes, [his line] ruling their masses for generations.
proposals.reason: 號十姓部落，世統其眾 names the people as the Ten Surname Tribes; the literal rendering makes Shidianmi himself 'called the Ten Surname Tribes'.

proposals.before: His clansman Buzhen wished to set himself up as qaghan and plotted to kill more than twenty of Mishe's younger brothers and nephews.
proposals.after: His elder clan brother Buzhen wished to set himself up as qaghan and plotted to kill more than twenty of Mishe's younger brothers and nephews.
proposals.reason: 族兄 specifies an elder brother of the same clan; 'clansman' drops the seniority stated in the Chinese (the literal field keeps 'clansman elder brother').

proposals.before: He rose through appointments to Grand General of the Right Xiaowei Guards, succeeded his father as Khan Irbis She, and served as Commissioner for Pacification and Solicitation of the Ten Surnames.
proposals.after: He rose through appointments to Grand General of the Right Xiaowei Guards, succeeded his father as Qaghan Xingxiwang, and served as Commissioner for Pacification and Solicitation of the Ten Surnames.
proposals.reason: 興昔亡可汗 is rendered 'Qaghan Xingxiwang' in s0181 and s0203; 'Khan Irbis She' is a wrong rendering of the inherited title.

proposals.before: He rose through appointments to Grand General of the Right Xiaowei Guards, succeeded his father as Khan Irbis She, and served as Commissioner for Pacification and Solicitation of the Ten Surnames.

proposals.before: Xian's homeland was gradually encroached upon by Ashina Mochuo and Wuzhile.
proposals.after: Xian's homeland was gradually encroached upon by Mochuo and Wuzhile.
proposals.reason: The Chinese reads only 默啜; 'Ashina' is not in the source text.

proposals.before: Ashina Bozhen had been appointed Grand General of the Left Tunwei Guards in his own realm.
proposals.after: Ashina Buzhen had been appointed Grand General of the Left Tunwei Guards in his own realm.
proposals.reason: 步真 is romanized 'Buzhen' throughout (s0182, s0195, s0204); 'Bozhen' obscures that this is the same Ashina Buzhen.

proposals.before: Together with Mishshe he helped subdue Helu and was further appointed General of Agile Cavalry, Acting Grand General of the Right Guards, Protector of Mengchi, and Khan Jiwangjue, with charge of the five Nishibi tribes.
proposals.after: Together with Mishe he helped subdue Helu and was further appointed General of Agile Cavalry, Acting Grand General of the Right Guards, Protector of Mengchi, and Khan Jiwangjue, with charge of the five Nishibi tribes.
